title: All is one simple will: from the will to emanate to the turning of the stars
overview: Chapters 53 and 54 are, he says, the two hardest of the book: no more *meshalim*, but the actual thing, how the physical world comes into being. Chapter 53 sums up the whole contemplation. From the will to emanate down to the will for the last deed in *Asiya* it is one simple will, as a person's will for a thing comes up all at once; in the *Kesarim* there are no differences of level, so a person doing a *mitzva* is literally doing the will of the *Aibershter*. What He wanted was not *Atzilus*, which is no big deal, nor the world, nor even *Yachid*, but that a person below do His will of his own free will: "I said and My will was done." To the Essence, *Atzilus* and *Asiya* are the same thing. So the stars move by His will, not by inertia, as a cartoon moves only when the next frame is painted, and the angels, the spheres and even the seventy princes of the nations are in *bittul* to Him like a horse to its rider. Bilaam could not go against His word, and Haman's rebellion made Purim. Next comes the side opposite holiness.

sections.title: One simple will, from the will to emanate down to the last deed
sections.summary: These two chapters are the actual thing, not a *mashal* (analogy): how the physical world comes into being. In the *Kesarim* (crowns) there are no differences of level, so the will for the last physical deed is the same simple will as the will to emanate, down to a person doing a *mitzva*.

phrases.he: (נג) ואחר כל הנזכר לעיל יובן למשכיל כללות כל ההתבוננות, מרצון הפשוט העצמי שבעצמות אור אין סוף ממש, מחמת בחינת חפץ חסד העצמי שעלה ברצונו הפשוט כו' (כנזכר לעיל באות יו"ד), עד בחינת הרצון היותר אחרון, שהוא בחינת הרצון להתהוות עולם העשיה בכלל ובפרט, שנקרא כתר ועתיק יומין דעשיה, והוא מה שכתוב כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה עשה
דודאי כמו שעלה ברצונו להיות חפץ ורצון להאציל, כך עלה חפץ ורצון זה לברוא, וחפץ ורצון ליצר, וחפץ ורצון לעשות, הכל היה כלול בעצם רצונו הפשוט שבעצמותו

blocks.text: Chapters 53 and 54 are the two hardest chapters of the book. Here there are no more *meshalim* (analogies): this is the actual thing. Understood properly, these two chapters bring the whole unity down into physicality, so that a person could do magic. Not magic, but like *kabbala maasis* (practical Kabbala): he could literally walk through walls, because they explain exactly how the whole thing works.
blocks.outOfPlace: His introduction to chapters 53 and 54, before the first line is read.

blocks.title: The four parts of Shaar HaYichud
blocks.text: *Shaar HaYichud* (the Gate of Unity), as Rabbi Markel told a young man he learned with one *Shabbos*, has four parts: a continuation of *Kuntres HaHispaalus* (the Tract on Ecstasy); *Kuntres HaHisbonenus* (the Tract on Contemplation), chapters one to six; the *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent), general in seven to nine and particular from ten on; and "the way of life" of "a *mitzva* is a lamp and the Torah is light". The book ends where the way of life begins, with the *yetzer hara* (evil inclination): chapter 54 is the *Satan* and the *kelipos* (husks) down to the primordial serpent, and its last words are "and the spirit of impurity I will remove entirely".
blocks.outOfPlace: His introduction to chapters 53 and 54, before the first line is read.

blocks.text: These two chapters need a very great *iyun* (close analysis). They come at the end of the *yichuda tata'a* (lower unity), and really they are not even that: the *yichuda tata'a* is finished. *Yichuda ila'a* (the higher unity) is how the *sefiros* (Divine attributes) of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation) are included in *Malchus* (kingship) of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite); *yichuda tata'a* is how the *sefiros* of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* are included in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*. What comes now is the world of the *kelipos*, the *inyan* (matter) of *kabbala maasis*: how the actual physical world comes into being.
blocks.outOfPlace: His introduction to chapters 53 and 54, before the first line is read.

blocks.title: Turning lead into gold
blocks.text: All of science is included in these two chapters, and all the magical systems: the occult sciences that Bilaam and Balak knew, the philosopher's stone, alchemy. A recent chapter even mentioned it: "The One who told the oil to burn will tell the vinegar to burn," which was said to be a bigger miracle than turning oil into vinegar. That is the alchemist's turning lead into gold. Its real, inner meaning is *merira l'misika*, turning bitter into sweet, which is called *is'hapcha* (transformation): nobody could come out of there, he was told, except one who can turn darkness into light and bitterness into sweetness. But there is also the literal thing: if you know how, you can change the *tzirufim* (combinations of letters). A *tzaddik* can do anything; a *tzaddik* can literally change the world around.
blocks.outOfPlace: His introduction to chapters 53 and 54, before the first line is read.

blocks.text: At the end of the last chapter he already finished, all the way down to where the physical thing comes out of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. Now he explains a little more, and the first two lines are read straight through: from the *ratzon hapashut* (simple will) in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) down to the last will, for the world of *Asiya*, all included in His simple will.

phrases.he: על דרך משל אדם שעלה ברצונו העצמי להיות לו רצון
לאיזה ענין דבר מה,
שאף על פי שבפרט הרי מיד הוא בא בחילוקי רצונות ממדריגה למדריגה, עד בחינת הרצון היותר אחרון
שהוא בחינת רצון לסוף מעשה ממש,
מכל מקום הכל עלה בבת אחת בעצם רצונו כו', מבלי חילוק מדריגות כלל

blocks.title: A person's one will for a thing
blocks.text: A person's essential will is to have a will **for a certain thing**. In detail it breaks at once into wills, level after level, down to the last will, the will **for the actual thing itself**; yet all of it came up at once in the essence of his will. So in the *etzem haratzon* (essence of the will) there is *mamash* (actually) no division of wills in the *Kesarim* (crowns) between the will to emanate and the will for the actual physical thing.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב באות ז', שאין חילוקי מדריגות בבחינת הכתרים דאבי"ע,
phrases.en: Really in the *Kesarim* there's no *chilukei madreigos* at all.

phrases.he: אף על פי שבהשתלשלות מבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון כו')

blocks.text: In the *Kesarim* there are no *chilukei madreigos* (differences of level) at all, though in the chain the *Malchus* of the upper becomes the *Keser* of the lower. The *Keser* of *Asiya* is just as high as the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, down to the particulars of our own will: the *Keser* of a person is literally the *Keser* of the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d). More than that, from the *Keser* of *Atzilus* to the will for the thing itself, it is literally the *ratzon hapashut*.

This is what the *mitzvos* are all about, "make His will as your will". Doing a *mitzva*, a person is literally doing the will of the *Aibershter*; doing an *aveira* (sin), he is literally going against it. As the *Tanya* says, it is like taking the king's head and putting it in the toilet. And this reaches the very last will, the most particular will in a person, who is called a whole world.

sections.title: I am first and I am last: what He really wanted
sections.summary: The will to emanate and the will for the lowest world are one will. And what He wanted was neither *Atzilus* nor the world nor even *Yachid* (the first of the three levels), which are all a descent, but that a person below do His will of his own free will: "I said and My will was done."

phrases.he: כך לגבי עצמות רצונו הפשוט שבבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף, אין חילוק מדריגות בין חפץ ורצון להאציל, בין חפץ ורצון לעשות כו'

וזהו אני ראשון, ברצון שבמלכות דאין סוף, מקור הרצון להאציל, ואני אחרון, ברצון האחרון שבמלכות דעשיה להתהוות עולם השפל היותר אחרון, שהן האופנים והמזלות, שהמה שרשי התהוות רוחניות הד' יסודות דאש רוח מים ועפר ורוחניות דומם צומח חי הגשמיים

blocks.text: The main thing He wanted, even more than to make the lower worlds, is why a Jew is *tofes* (takes hold) in the essence of the *ratzon hapashut*, in the Essence of the *Aibershter*. As the *Tanya* of the last few days said, a *mitzva* takes hold of the Essence even more than *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) does, because it is the essence of the simple will. But remember that it also says the learning of *Chassidus* is itself a *mitzva*, a very lofty one, the biggest of them all: it is *talmud Torah*, which equals them all, and the inner part of the Torah itself.

What He really wanted was not even to make the world, and not even to make the Jew. The reason He made the Jew is so that the Jew should do His will of his own free will. That is what comes next: the creation of the *Satan*. He made it possible for a person to do His will, and this is the biggest miracle of them all.

blocks.title: Scratching his head
blocks.text: *Atzilus* is not such a big miracle. It is like a person scratching his head, not even that: would you say, wow, what a genius, he can scratch his head? *Atzilus* is a *yerida* (descent). Even its highest levels: wow, He can make angels! That is an insult. To say of the *Aibershter* that He can make *Atzilus*: so what? The whole thing was to make the person, and not even to make the person for the sake of having people.
That is why the *goyim* (non-Jews) are not intrinsic. They are only extrinsic, and the whole world is extrinsic; it really does not need to exist at all.

sensitivity.reason: Says non-Jews are not intrinsic to creation, only extrinsic.
sensitivity.publishable: The whole world is extrinsic; it really does not need to exist at all.

blocks.text: Most people think it is such a beautiful world and G-d wanted it so much. No: He does not need a world; the world is a *yerida*, a hassle, and even for us a lousy place. The beautiful trees are nothing. See the beauty of only the *heichalos* (chambers) of *Asiya*, by the *Ofanim* (a class of angels), and you will never look at a tree again: the trees will look ugly to you.

People think G-d loves the world and loves people, and that is why He made them. He would not have to make people; He would have destroyed the world at the giving of the Torah: "If you accept the Torah, fine. If not, I'm going to destroy it all. What do I need it for?" There is no intrinsic value in the world per se, absolutely none. It is not a wonderful world full of love, motherhood and the like: what do you need motherhood for? As you go up, even the love of a mother in *Asiya* is a bigger thing, and you would not think of these things anymore. Or that Chinese food and shish kebab: just for that it was worth having a world? Absolutely not true. The taste of the food is part of the evil.

sensitivity.reason: Dismisses motherhood ("what do you need motherhood for?") and calls the taste of food part of the evil; a reader could take it as contempt for mothers and ordinary life.
sensitivity.publishable: People think G-d loves the world and loves people, and that is why He made them. He would not have to make people; He would have destroyed the world at the giving of the Torah: "If you accept the Torah, fine. If not, I'm going to destroy it all. What do I need it for?" There is no intrinsic value in the world per se, absolutely none. It is not a wonderful world full of love: as you go up, even the love of a mother in *Asiya* is a bigger thing, and you would not think of these things anymore. Or that Chinese food and shish kebab: just for that it was worth having a world? Absolutely not true. The taste of the food is part of the evil.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Whether "what do you need motherhood for?" is only his delivery, or part of the teaching that the world's goods are nothing beside the higher worlds; the taste of food as part of the evil is kept in both texts as his position.

blocks.text: Or the beautiful scenery: camping, the sunset, the trees, the birds singing. What does the *Mishna* say? Someone walking on the road reviewing his *Mishna* who says, "What a beautiful tree," is liable for his life. The *Aibershter* says, "I might as well kill you. What do I need you here for? To look at the trees? To smell the flowers? That's what I made you for?" This whole world is the lowest world, with none lower than it.

And this can be said not only of this world but of *Atzilus*, of *Atik*, of *Adam Kadmon* (the first world), and in truth of *Yachid* (the first of the three levels). Who needs *Atik*? Get rid of it. Who needs *Yachid*? It is a bother; you don't need *Yachid* at all.

blocks.question: Wow, the Essence, *Yachid, Echad, Kadmon*: what do you mean He doesn't need *Yachid*?
blocks.text: *Yachid* is the light that reveals the *Aibershter* within Himself. But He needs no light: of Him it says, "Darkness is as light." He knew everything that was going on there without *Yachid*. The whole reason for *Yachid* was to end up with us, so even *Yachid* is a *yerida*.

There is higher than *Yachid*, and higher than that, and even that is a *yerida*. So what did He want? "*Nachas ruach* (gratification) before Me, that I said and My will was done." Rabbi Markel had just read it in the daily lessons, in the *Tanya* or a *Rashi*; he did not remember where.

That is what it was all about. G-d saw the whole world and it was "very good": "good" is the *yetzer tov* (good inclination), "very" is the *yetzer hara*. Very good means a person went against the *yetzer hara* and did the *Aibershter*'s will, *mamash* His will. And "he did My will" means not that he did what I wanted, but that he made My will: he did the actual will down here.

Since there is no *hishtalshelus* in the *Kesarim*, the *Aibershter* gave us the *ratzon ha'atzmi* (the essential will): putting on *tefillin*, we are literally acting for Him. As the *Tanya* of these days says, *davka* (specifically) the body does the will, not the soul, so the body, and the animal soul from *kelipas noga* (the husk that is mostly bad and a little good), becomes part of it. Then it is an open *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him): what the world was created for.

sections.title: To the Essence, Atzilus and Asiya are the same thing
sections.summary: "Whatever G-d wished, He did" includes the whole chain of the *Kav* (the line) to the end of *Asiya*, and calls all of it a deed, because to the Essence the root of *Atzilus* and the root of *Asiya* are the same. Even *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity), before the *tzimtzum* (contraction), is a deed to Him.

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב בסוף העץ חיים) שזהו נכלל הכל במה שכתוב כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה בעצמות עשה, שכולל כל ההשתלשלות דקו, עד סוף עולם העשיה, דהיינו שכוללם יחד
שנקרא הכל בבחינת עשיה לבד,
phrases.en: The whole thing, including *Atzilus*, is nothing but *Asiya* by Him.

phrases.he: כי שרש האצילות ושרש העשיה שוין ממש לגבי עצמותו כו'
phrases.en: It's the same thing by Him.

blocks.text: All is included in "Whatever G-d wished, He did in His Essence," which includes the whole chain of the *Kav* down to the end of *Asiya*. To Him the whole thing, *Atzilus* included, is nothing but *Asiya*: the root of *Atzilus* and the root of *Asiya* are **the same thing by Him**. Like a person and the cat, as a listener put it: to the *Aibershter*, *Atzilus* and *Asiya* are *mamash* the same thing.

phrases.he: וזהו עשה בשמים, סובב הכללי דטהירו עילאה, וטהירו תתאה וארץ דבחינת ממלא כל עלמין כו', הכל בהשוואה אחת
(כידוע דעקב דאדם קדמון שמסתיים בסוף העשיה וראשו במחשבה כללית בתחלת הקו, (וכמו באדם הראשון, שאמרו שקודם החטא היה רגליו בעשיה וראשו בבריאה (נקרא אדם דבריאה יש מאין כו')
(והיינו וכל קומה לפניך תשתחוה כו' כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: "He did, in the heavens and in the earth": the heavens are the *sovev* (encompassing light) of *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity), the earth *memalei kol almin* (the light that fills all worlds), all equal. To Him even *tehiru ila'a*, before the *tzimtzum*, what we called *Yachid*, is a deed. "Every stature shall bow before You" is the stature of *Adam Kadmon*.

sections.title: The point of the contemplation: He is making us right now, down to the stars
sections.summary: The aim of every detail of the contemplation is that all is included in the simple unity, down to Divine providence over the last detail. The stars do not move by inertia but by His simple will, and the spheres, angels and *Ofanim* of *Asiya* are in utter *bittul* (self-nullification).

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר המכוון בכל ההתבוננות, בכל פרט ופרט שבכל ההשתלשלות דקו, מלפני הצמצום הראשון עד סוף העשיה,
רק להיות נכלל הכל באחדות הפשוטה,
phrases.en: It's *mamash* the *Aibershter* all the way down to here.

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף עד שיקבע בנפש גם בסדר השגחה אלהי״ת בפרטיות, עד הפרט היותר אחרון

blocks.text: This is the main intent of all the contemplation, of every detail of the chain from before the first *tzimtzum* to the end of *Asiya*: that all be included in the simple unity. It is the *Aibershter* **all the way down to here**. The *Aibershter* is literally making us right now; forget the *hishtalshelus*. And it is to be fixed in the soul down to Divine providence over the very last detail.

phrases.he: שהוא גם בעולם הגלגלים והמזלות,
שהם רק מט' כלים החיצונים דמלכות דמלכות דעשיה, שהוא רק על פי רצונו הפשוט שבעצמות אור אין סוף ממש
וכמו שאנו אומרים, ומסדר את הכוכבים במשמרותיהם ברקיע כרצונו דוקא,
דהיינו כרצונו הפשוט שבעצמותו ממש
מטעם הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: The *galgalim* (celestial spheres) and *mazalos* (constellations), **our sky**, go only by the simple will in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, not by inertia. People think Mars was there yesterday and is here today because where else could it go: it is in its orbit, going on inertia, like a ball you throw. No: "He arranges the stars... according to His will." It is there right now because that is exactly where the *Aibershter* wants it, as **He Himself** wanted.

phrases.he: ופירוש במשמרותיהם, היינו גם בבחינת היכלות דקליפת נוגה דעשיה, שהמזלות הקבועים ברקיע, היינו בבחינת נוגה דעשיה
כי עשר ספירות דעשיה בבחינת אורות וכלים והיכלות כו', הכל הוא בבחינת ביטול היש לאין בתכלית, כידוע דבהיכל קודש קדשים דעשיה שם יחוד זעיר אנפין ונוקבא דעשיה, כמו בבית המקדש שלמטה כו'

blocks.text: What does "in their watches" mean? Not only the *heichalos* of *Asiya*: now we are talking about the *heichalos* of *kelipas noga* of *Asiya*, which are the *chalal*, the space of the physical world, where the constellations are fixed. The ten *sefiros* of *Asiya*, its lights, vessels and chambers, go down into the *noga* of *Asiya*, and all of it is in utter *bittul* of the *yesh* (something) to the *ayin* (nothing), as the union of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* of *Asiya* is in its Holy of Holies, as in the Temple below.

phrases.he: ונשמות ומלאכים דעשיה הן בתכלית הביטול כמו שכתוב וצבא השמים לך משתחוים, וכמו האופנים וחיות דעשיה
וגם חומר וכלי האופנים בבחינת הביטול בתכלית, וכמובן במרכבת יחזקאל בחיות ואופנים דיצירה

blocks.text: The souls and angels of *Asiya* are in utter *bittul*, as it says, "the host of heaven bows to You"; the stars and planets are connected to angels. Even the matter and vessel of the *Ofanim* are in utter *bittul*, as in Yechezkel's chariot: they can only do what the *Aibershter* makes them do.

sections.title: The kingdom dressed in the seventy princes: a horse under its rider
sections.summary: In exile *Malchus* is dressed in the seventy *sarim* (princes) of *noga*, which is why the nations rule; yet they are in utter *bittul* to Him, like a horse to its rider or an axe in the hand of the one who swings it. Even the last forty-eight *tzirufim* are under "G-d reigns over the nations", and with *Moshiach* the kingship will be dressed in the Jews.

phrases.he: וכך גם במרכבה דסוסים שחורים ואדומים דזכריה בזמן הגלות, שהמלכות מלובשת בע' שרים דנוגה דעשיה, גם הם בתכלית הביטול כסוס לגבי רוכב

blocks.text: So too the chariot of black and red horses in the time of the exile, where *Malchus* is dressed in the seventy *sarim* of the *noga* of *Asiya*: all the way down to what was just learned on Purim.

That is what the *Megilla* says: all the way to the seventy *sarim* and even the king, the whole thing is in the hands of the *Aibershter*. They thought they were doing what they wanted, but even Haman was doing what the *Aibershter* wanted. *Malchus* is dressed in the seventy *sarim* of *noga* instead of coming to us, and that is why the *goyim* have the kingship. Yet they too are in utter *bittul*, like a horse to its rider.

phrases.he: וכמו הנה יהו״ה רוכב על עב קל כו' וכמו שכתוב בזהר, כעננים למרכב כו' ועל דרך שאמר היתפאר הגרזן על החוצב בו כו'

blocks.text: "Behold, G-d rides on a swift cloud," and the *Zohar*'s clouds for a chariot: the *Aibershter* is riding on it. Even Arafat, Bin Laden and Bush, the different kingdoms, the kingdom of Yishmael and the kingdom of Edom, have *Malchus* of *Asiya* dressed in them, and what is happening is what the *Aibershter* wanted to happen right now.

sensitivity.reason: Names Arafat, Bin Laden and Bush together as the kingdoms of Yishmael and Edom.
sensitivity.publishable: "Behold, G-d rides on a swift cloud," and the *Zohar*'s clouds for a chariot: the *Aibershter* is riding on it. Even the rulers of today, the different kingdoms, the kingdom of Yishmael and the kingdom of Edom, have *Malchus* of *Asiya* dressed in them, and what is happening is what the *Aibershter* wanted to happen right now.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The kingdoms of Yishmael and Edom are the teaching; whether naming a US president beside Arafat and Bin Laden prints as said is a call on present-day politics.

blocks.title: The axe and the one who hews with it
blocks.text: "Shall the axe boast over the one who hews with it?" The *Aibershter* is holding them. If you get hit by the axe, who hit you? Like in Madrid: who hit Madrid? It was the *Aibershter*.

sensitivity.reason: Says of a real terror attack (Madrid) that it was G-d who struck.
sensitivity.publishable: "Shall the axe boast over the one who hews with it?" The *Aibershter* is holding them. If you get hit by the axe, who hit you? It was the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: והגם שיש בהם חילוקי מדריגות בהשתלשלות רבות עד אותן שמקבלים על ידי ריבוי מסכים מבחינת אחוריים דאחוריים דאלהי״ם, ממ"ח צירופים האחרונים שנקרא אדמת בני חם,
בתכלית ההסתר והצמצום בכמה מיני מסכים והבדלות עד שנקרא לבוש שק ועור, כמו אלביש שמים קדרות ושק אשים כסותם כו' כידוע,
וכמו שאמר המבדיל כו'
phrases.en: He makes a separation between the light and the darkness, between *Yisroel* and the *amim*.

phrases.he: מכל מקום נאמר מלך אלהי״ם על גוים כו'
phrases.en: Nonetheless, really the *Aibershter* is the king even over the *goyim*.

phrases.he: מי לא ייראך מלך הגוים כו' שמלכותו בכל משלה

blocks.text: There are many levels, down to those that receive through many screens from the back of the back of *Elokim*, the last forty-eight *tzirufim*, called "the land of the children of Cham". There are a hundred and twenty *tzirufim* of *Elokim*, twenty-four for each letter: seventy-two that start with *alef*, *lamed* and *heh*, the *tzirufim* of holiness, and forty-eight that start with *yud* and *mem*. Those last forty-eight are the lowest of the *tzirufim*, "the land of the children of Cham": Cham is forty-eight. They are in utter concealment, behind many screens, down to sackcloth. And "He who separates": **between the light and the darkness**, between the Jews and the nations.

**Nonetheless**, "G-d reigns over the nations": the *Aibershter* is king even over the *goyim*. Part of the coming of *Moshiach* is that they accept this kingship, with the commandments of the children of Noach, and accept *Moshiach* as their kaiser. Then *Malchus* will be dressed not in the seventy *sarim* but *davka* in the Jews: the kingship of the earth like the kingship of heaven. "His kingship rules over all."

sections.title: Bilaam, his donkey and the impure kelipos: no one goes against His will
sections.summary: Bilaam, from the evil of *noga*, could not go against G-d's word, and neither could his donkey. Even the three entirely impure *kelipos*, who know their Master and rebel, are subdued at times, and their rebellion is still within His will: Haman made Purim.

phrases.he: וראיה מבלעם, שהיה מבחינת רע דנוגה, בחינת דעת דקליפה כמו שכתוב ויודע דעת עליון כו',
אמר לא אוכל לעבור את פי יהו״ה לעשות קטנה כו'
phrases.en: I really can't do nothing against the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: (וגם מאתונו בחינת נוקבא דזעיר אנפין דקליפה, שהיא יותר קשה (כמו שיתבאר שבאת זה לעומת זה בחינת הנוקבא יותר קשה מכולם כו')
כתיב ותט האתון כו'
phrases.en: She moved away from the angel.

phrases.he: וגם בלעם אמר אם רע בעיניך אשובה לי כו')
phrases.en: If you don't want me to do it, I'll go back.

blocks.text: The proof is Bilaam, who was from the evil of *noga*, *daas* (knowledge) of *kelipa*. He was not from the three impure *kelipos* but from the evil of *noga*, which is the root of the three *kelipos*. He "knew the knowledge of the Most High," and he said he could not go against the word of G-d: **I really can't do nothing**. Not that he did not want to; he wanted to.

So too his donkey, the *Nukva* of *Zeir Anpin* of *kelipa*, which is harder: in the side opposite holiness the *Nukva* is the worst thing there is. "And the donkey turned aside": **she moved away from the angel**. And Bilaam too said, "If it is bad in your eyes, I will go back": **if you don't want me to do it, I'll go back**.

phrases.he: והגם שיש מהם שהן בבחינת יש נפרד גמור לומר כחי ועוצם ידי כו',
phrases.en: There's *goyim* that are totally *nifrad l'gamrei*: there is no *Aibershter* at all, and we are doing it ourselves.

phrases.he: כמו שר של מצרים שאמר לי יאורי כו' וכמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה יודעים את רבונם ומתכוונין למרוד בו,
הנה זהו מבחינת ג' קליפות הטמאות לגמרי, וגם הם נכנעים לפרקים כאשר יפקוד יהו״ה עליהם
כמבואר בנבואת הנביאים על כמה שרי אומות העולם כו'

blocks.text: But wait a minute: there are *goyim* who are entirely separate, who say "my strength and the might of my hand": there is no G-d at all, and **we are doing it ourselves**. Like the prince of Egypt who said "my river is mine", and as the Sages say, they know their Master and intend to rebel against Him: there are people like that. They are from the three entirely impure *kelipos*, and they too are subdued at times, when G-d visits them, as the prophets foretell of the princes of the nations. These three are totally separate and want to go against the *Aibershter*, and even they cannot really go against Him.

The worst of all the *kelipos*, Haman, actually going against it and trying to destroy the Jews, originated the holiday of Purim for us, the highest of all the holidays: think of Yom Kippurim. So even those who are not subdued and go against His will are still within His will.

sections.title: The song of the spheres: there is no inertia
sections.summary: Even *noga* of *Asiya* is always in *bittul*: the spheres, the seventy *sarim*, bow and sing every day, and that song, not inertia, is why the matter of the spheres turns. Up to here everything is one and nothing happens unless He does it; next comes the side opposite holiness.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת נגה, גם בבחינת נגה דעשיה שרובו רע ומיעוטו טוב, המה בבחינת ביטול תמיד,
כמו הגלגלים והמזלות שהן ע' שרים דכתיב בהם גם כן וצבא השמים לך משתחוים
ואומרים שירה בכל יום כו'
phrases.en: And they have to sing every day to the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: וכידוע בענין הטעם לסיבוב התמידי דחומר הגלגלים, שהוא רק מצד השירה שאומרים, בחינת הצורה ונפש הגלגל בהשתחוואה רוחנית כו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר ודי למבין

blocks.text: But *noga*, even the *noga* of *Asiya*, which is mostly bad and a little good, is always in *bittul*, like the *galgalim* and *mazalos*, the seventy *sarim*, of whom it also says "the host of heaven bows to You": they **have to sing every day**. The constant turning of the matter of the spheres is only because of the song their form and soul say in spiritual bowing. The world is not going around because of inertia, as people think. There is no such thing as inertia, actually.

blocks.title: The cartoon with no inertia
blocks.text: It is like a cartoon. If you do not paint the next frame, the guy will not move forward. The guy in the cartoon hits the baseball and the ball flies. Why is it flying? He hit it, it's inertia! What are you talking about? There is no inertia in a cartoon. If the artist would not paint the next ball, it would stop right there.
So the matter of the *galgalim* moves because of the *shira* (song) that the form and soul of the *galgal*, the inner angel of the star, is saying.

blocks.title: The music of the spheres
blocks.text: There is an actual theory like that: the magnetic stuff that holds everything together is like a song, vibrations *mamash* like music, the music of the spheres. In the days of *Avraham Avinu* (Abraham our father) they knew how to hear what goes on upstairs. That is why the camp of Sancheriv freaked out: they were made to hear, not the music of the angels, only the music of the spheres, the planets and stars turning around.

Up to here he explains, all the way down, that it is all one thing and nothing happens unless the *Aibershter* does it. The next chapter is the *hishtalshelus* of the *zeh l'umas zeh* (this opposite that), the main thing He wanted: a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), with a *kelipa* to go against, so that the Jew overcomes the *kelipa* and does the will of the *Aibershter*.

Turning to chapter 54 and the *yetzer hara*, he sings a song he calls someone's original: "The *yetzer hara* is a friend of mine, we get together and we dine, and we have a glass of wine, 'cause the *yetzer hara* is a friend of mine."

reviewQuestions.question: How does the *mashal* of a person who wants a thing show that the will to emanate and the will for the last deed are one will?
Why is the *Keser* of *Asiya*, and even a person's will, as high as the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, and what does that mean for a *mitzva* and an *aveira*?
If the world, *Atzilus* and even *Yachid* are a *yerida*, what did the *Aibershter* really want?
Why do the stars move, according to the line "He arranges the stars in their watches according to His will", and what does the cartoon show?
How do Bilaam, his donkey and Haman show that even the *kelipos* cannot go against His will?

notes.text: Lines 1-2, 5-11, 15-20, 25 and 27 are read in Hebrew without English; their phrases have no en. Line 12's en is his "means is mamash the Aibershter all the way down to here"; line 21's fourth phrase joins his "nonetheless" (w468) to his gloss "so really the Aibershter is the king even over the goyim" (w480-492); line 24's first phrase cites w786-810, his rendering with some of the Hebrew inside it.

Right after line 6 he reads the verse of line 7 (w1311-1321) and then talks for some twenty minutes (w1322-2959) on what He really wanted; he comes back and reads line 7 at w2960. The talk is placed under lines 5-6.

w2614-2699: he searches for where "nachas ruach lefanai she'amarti v'naasa retzoni" is (the daily lessons, the Tanya or a Rashi; "Shaarei Orah" is suggested from the room). It is Rashi on Vayikra 1:9. The block keeps his not remembering.
w1221-1246: "a person who's called a עולם מלא" may be a mishearing of olam katan (a small world); the block says "a whole world".

w553-587: the miracle of the vinegar that burned (Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, Taanis 25a), cited as from "the last chapter or the one before"; "this is actually a bigger miracle than to turn the oil into vinegar" is kept as transcribed, though he may mean that making vinegar burn is the bigger miracle. Who said "nobody could come out of here except one who can turn darkness into light" to whom (w628-655) is not said.
Line 16: he reads "shelemaala" and corrects himself to "shelemata" (w3514-3519). Line 18: he reads "to'ar" for "chomer", is corrected from the room and says his text has to'ar (w3552-3566).
Line 22: the line says Bilaam was from the evil of noga; that noga is "the root of the three kelipos" is his (w650-668).
Line 25: "Yom Kippurim, you know" (w927-931) is not explained; presumably the play on Yom Kippurim as a day "like Purim". The block only points at it.

Class 232 has Sofer's word times, and opens mid-thought on line 19 (the Megilla and Haman, w0-56), continuing class 231's "what we just learned on Purim". The aside on Arafat, Bin Laden, Bush and Madrid dates the class to about 2004.

People written out: the young man he learned with that Shabbos (w129-162); "like you said, you and the cat" (w3019) is a listener's earlier example; the song's author, named in class (w1543-1550), is left unnamed ("someone's original").
